text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: real-time p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (hosted-us-west). p95 up 350%, p99 up 820% vs baseline. paging oncall.
monitoring-bot: Alert rule: realtime-latency-p99-breach (threshold 1.2s). Window: last 2m. Affected pods: 12/48 exceed 1.2s.
Mike: oncall-sre here, ACK. Looking at dashboard now -> https://grafana.redwood/boards/latency-live
Arya: oncall-ml joining. Any recent rollouts? I see a canary for kv-cache v2 pushed ~20m ago (traffic split 10%).
Jess: infra - no infra deploys in last hour from my side. Autoscaler shows spike in queue length though.
Nora: Product-Alerts: we see a customer-reported slow responses in app UX (session id starts with a7f3). Impacting ~3% of requests but users see spinner >5s.
Sanjay: eng-runtime - checking model routing logs. Noticed elevated tail lat for model-large-quant. Some routes fell back to it during capacity pressure.
Mike: Quick triage steps: 1) confirm scope (hosts, region, model), 2) check recent deploys/rollouts, 3) runbook checks (eviction, GC, memory), 4) mitigations (fallbacks, routing, scale).
Arya: Dashboard notes: KV cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 21% around 4023456600. That lines up with spike start.
Mike: Could be cold cache or cache invalidation bug from kv-cache v2 rollout. Arya can you verify cache replica logs?
Arya: Running quick query on cache-service: ``grep -R "invalidate" /var/log/kvcache | tail -n 200``. Seeing frequent invalidation requests for prefix ids from canary controller.
Jess: infra: Autoscaler added no new nodes because reserved capacity pools hit limit (dedicated pools partially saturated). We can enable burst capacity but will take ~45s to spin up.
Sanjay: Meanwhile streaming tails show stalls on streaming shard 18. Per-request timeouts increased; KV cache miss causes runtime to re-evaluate entire prompt leading to long compute.
Mike: Immediate mitigation plan (fast actions):
- Abort/rollback kv-cache v2 canary (if safe)
- Temporarily route traffic away from model-large-quant to model-small-fp16 for latency-sensitive routes
- Enable burst capacity in us-west for Dedicated pool
- Reduce batch size for /v1/generate in prod -> from 8 to 4
Who's owning each? I'll take rollback + routing exec.
Arya: I'll confirm whether canary rollback will cause further cache churn. If canary controller has an invalidation bug, rolling back may spike invalidations again. Need controlled step: pause controller, then rollback binary.
Mike: Good call. Jess, can you enable burst capacity and set desired to +20%? Callout: cost spike acceptable for mitigation.
Jess: Enabling burst now. API: ``POST /dedicated/scale?region=us-west&delta=+20`` -> job queued 4023456921. ETA ~40s.
Nora: Customer ops: which customers are impacted? We have a backbone customer on dedicated pool (acme-corp) and several hosted customers. I can message CS to prep comms for acme-corp if we expect >10m degrade.
Sanjay: Routing change: updating routing policy to prefer model-small-fp16 for SLAs flagged "latency-sensitive". Patch:
```
route "latency-sensitive" -> model-small-fp16
fallback -> model-small-int8
```
Applying now with immediate priority.
Mike: Also toggle auto-fallback policy to prefer region fallback before model fallback to avoid cross-region latency. Set fallback window to 15s.
Arya: I'm pausing canary controller to stop invalidations. Command: ``kubectl -n infra scale deployment/kv-canary-controller --replicas=0``. Done.
Arya: Now initiating conservative rollback of kv-cache v2 binary from 10% -> 0% over 2 steps to avoid double-invalidations.
monitoring-bot: Deployment event: kv-cache canary scaled to 0 replicas at 4023457002.
Mike: Good. After pause + routing + burst, check p95/p99 in next 2 mins.
monitoring-bot: Metric stream: p95 trending down from 1.4s -> 0.9s (1min) ; p99 from 2.8s -> 1.1s (1.5min)
Nora: Product-Alerts: UX reports improving; affected sessions dropping to ~0.8%.
Sanjay: Streaming shard 18 queue drained after routing change. Stalls reduced; per-shard latency back to baseline.
Arya: KV cache hit rate recovering: 21% -> 62% after pause and rollback start.
Mike: Mitigation successful so far. Next steps: full rollback of kv-cache v2, run canary controller fix in staging, add stricter canary invalidation throttles, add alert on sudden cache-hit drops.
Jess: Burst capacity is up. Autoscaler logs: nodes added (3/3). Job completed 4023457059.
Product-Alerts: Notifying customer success for acme-corp; suggested message: "Experiencing elevated latencies in us-west between 12:11-12:16 PST, mitigations applied, monitoring continuing." Approve?
Nora: Approve, I'll send.
Mike: Post-incident actions (PIA):
- Root cause: canary controller sent broad invalidations due to bad pattern matching -> cache churn -> runtime recompute -> tail latency
- Action items: canary controller fix, add cache-hit drop alert, simulate canary invalidation in canary tests, add safer rollout strategy (ramp down invalidations), refine routing fallback order
- Owner: Arya (kv cache fix), Sanjay (routing fallback config), Jess (autoscale runbooks), Mike (postmortem)
Arya: Agree. I'll open PR with tests and ETA EOD.
Sanjay: I'll update routing policy docs and add a playbook for forced-route quick steps.
Mike: Any lingering user impact? monitoring-bot: current affected requests 0.3%, p99 stable ~0.95s.
Nora: CS queue patched; no escalations. Closing conference bridge in 10m unless regressions.
ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Severity downgraded from Sev2 -> Sev4 (monitoring). Logged incident id: INC-2026-042
Mike: Thanks team. I'll draft initial incident summary and ping for postmortem scheduling.
Arya: Noting sla window for acme-corp: log shows 12:10-12:16 PST as degrade. I'll attach traces.
Jess: Will follow up with capacity recommendation to avoid future dedicated pool saturation.
Product-Alerts: Closing thread for now. React with :thumbsup: when done.
notes: runbook steps executed: pause canary controller, partial rollback, routing override, enable burst capacity, reduce batch size. Postmortem owner: Mike. Times in event correspond to thread_ts window.
